# instantiation_paren_follow_prettier_divergence

Prettier strips the paren pair around an instantiation expression whatever token follows it; tsv keeps the pair when that token would re-lex the closing `>`.

tsv: `(fn<T>) + 1`, `(fn<T>) >= 1`, `(fn<T>)!`
Prettier: `fn<T> + 1`, `fn<T> >= 1`, `fn<T>!`

## Reason

**Semantic preservation.** A type argument list is only read as one when the token after its `>` cannot continue a comparison chain. Prettier's `fn<T> + 1` re-parses as `fn < T > +1` — a different program, and prettier's own second pass prints it that way. Its `fn<T> < 1`, `fn<T> > 1`, `fn<T> >= 1`, `fn<T> >> 1`, `fn<T> >>> 1` and `fn<T>!` do not parse at all under tsc — `'>' expected` on the first, `Expression expected` on the other five. tsc's rule (`canFollowTypeArgumentsInExpression`): a `<`, `>`, `+` or `-` token never follows a type argument list, and a `!` starts an expression, so it does not either. acorn-typescript, tsv's parse oracle, additionally rejects `<<` there (`fn<T> << 1`, which tsc reads as an instantiation), so the pair stays ahead of `<<` too. Every other binary operator can follow one, so the pair strips there — the set `instantiation_operator_follow` pins from the bare side, alongside the `input_invalid_*` files carrying the followers neither parser admits.

The axis is the join of two tokens, not the operand's node: an operand that merely ends on the close (`a * fn<T> + 1`, `-fn<T> + 1`, `<T>fn<U> + 1`) re-lexes the same way, so the pair wraps that whole operand, and a pair authored around the instantiation alone moves out to it (`unformatted_ours_inner_pair`). The walk stops at a child that takes its own pair there by precedence — an inner assertion ends the operand on a `)`, so `<T>(<U>fn<V>) + 1` needs none, and both formatters agree.

**The bare spellings tsv repairs, and why the template carries them.** Two of those followers parse bare under acorn-typescript — tsv's parse oracle, and the parser Svelte itself uses — where tsc's grammar rejects them: `fn<T> < 1` (tsc: `'>' expected`) and `fn<T> >= 1` (tsc: `Expression expected`) are instantiation expressions to acorn, so tsv accepts them and the formatter repairs them, printing `(fn<T>) < 1` and `(fn<T>) >= 1` — the same tree in the spelling tsc, acorn and tsv all read alike. Accepting therefore costs nothing downstream, while rejecting would refuse a `<script lang="ts">` Svelte compiles today.

The two parsers prettier runs over one component are what make that repair oracle-visible. `prettier-plugin-svelte` snips every `<script>` / `<style>` body out of the source before Svelte's parser sees it (`snipScriptAndStyleTagContent` substitutes `{}` / `''`), so Svelte parses only the markup — a template expression is acorn-typescript's, and both bare spellings survive there — while the snipped-out body goes to prettier's own TypeScript parser, which is tsc's and throws (`'>' expected.`), so no `<script>` line can hold one. That is why the bare side lives in the template: `unformatted_ours_bare_follow` bares `{fn<T> < 1}` and `{fn<T> >= 1}`, tsv puts the pair back (landing on `input.svelte`), and prettier keeps them bare (landing on `output_prettier.svelte`), both halves graded against the live oracles.

`fn<T> << 1` is the mirror (tsc's instantiation, acorn's reject) and repairs the same way, but the fixture path does not carry it. The bare spelling is not a tsv fixed point, so it cannot be an `input.*`. In the template — where the bare followers above have to live — it cannot be a variant either: Svelte's own parser rejects the cell, so prettier throws on the whole component (`https://svelte.dev/e/js_parse_error`) where N6 needs it to LAND on some form other than input, and the same rejection leaves `svelte compile` nothing to render, so the render-equivalence oracle every `.svelte` variant is graded against has nothing to say. A `<script lang="ts">` spelling escapes only the first of those — prettier reads that body with tsc's parser, which takes `fn<T> << 1` — and still fails the second, since the component as a whole is one Svelte's parser rejects. That repair, and the `+` / `-` contrast that bounds the class (both parsers read `fn<T> + 1` as the chain `fn < T > +1`, so tsv prints the chain rather than repairing anything, and a third form is not a variant's input), are pinned in [`tests/instantiation_follow_parens.rs`](../../../../../instantiation_follow_parens.rs).

See [conformance_prettier.md](../../../../../../docs/conformance_prettier.md) §Prettier bug index and [conformance_prettier_ts.md](../../../../../../docs/conformance_prettier_ts.md) §TypeScript (Instantiation expression parens).
